gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type the preposition of movement: to, into, out of, onto, off, through, across, along, up, down, past, towards, over or round. Twenty original sentences.

questions.explain: Movement towards a destination: to school. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.before: She opened the door and walked
questions.explain: From outside to inside a space: into the classroom.

questions.after: the building when the bell rang.
questions.explain: From inside to outside: out of the building. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Movement to a surface: onto the table. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.after: the bus at the next stop.
questions.explain: Leaving a bus, train or plane: get off. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Entering a car or taxi: get into the car. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Leaving a car or taxi: out of. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.after: a long tunnel under the mountain.
questions.explain: Inside a space from one end to the other: through.
A space with trees all around: through the forest.
From one side of a flat surface to the other: across.

questions.after: the river to the other bank.
questions.explain: Side to side over water: across the river. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Following the length of a line: along the beach. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Movement to a higher place: up the stairs. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Movement to a lower place: down the hill. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Moving beside something and beyond it: past. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
In the direction of: towards. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
From one side to the other above something: over. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Below something: under the bridge. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
In a circle: round (around) the lake. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
No ‘to’ before ‘home’: we went home. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

wordOrder.title: Put it in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words to build each sentence — 20 examples with prepositions of movement.

matching.title: Match the movement and the preposition
matching.subtitle: Tap a movement, then tap the preposition that describes it.

pairs.left: jump to the top of a table
go from one side of a road to the other

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. To = destination, into / out of = inside / outside, through = inside a space, across = over a surface or line.

questions.text: She opened the door and went        the kitchen.
wrongReasons: ‘To the kitchen’ is the destination, but ‘into’ shows the movement of entering.
‘Onto’ is for moving to a surface.
‘Through’ means passing from one side to the other.
questions.explain: Entering a space: into the kitchen. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: The fish jumped        the water.
wrongReasons: ‘Off’ is for surfaces and public transport.
‘Outside’ is a position, not this movement.
questions.explain: From inside to outside: out of. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: We have to get        the train at the next station.
wrongReasons: ‘Out of’ is for cars and taxis.
questions.explain: Leaving a train, bus or plane: get off. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: The cat jumped        the wall.
wrongReasons: ‘Into the wall’ would mean inside it.
questions.explain: Moving to a surface: onto. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: Look left and right before you walk        the road.
wrongReasons: ‘Through’ is for spaces with sides, like a tunnel.
‘Along’ means following the length of the road.
questions.explain: Side to side over a flat surface: across. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: The train went        a long tunnel.
questions.explain: Inside a space from end to end: through. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: We walked        the river for an hour.
questions.explain: Following a line: along. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: She climbed        the ladder to fix the light.
wrongReasons: ‘Over’ means from one side to the other.
‘Onto’ is for the surface you land on.
questions.explain: Moving higher: up. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: Walk        the bakery and the bank is on your right.
questions.explain: Going by something: past. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: The dog came running        me.
questions.explain: In the direction of: towards. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: The horse jumped        the fence.
questions.explain: Above and to the other side: over. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: It’s late — let’s go       .
wrongReasons: ‘At home’ is a position, not movement.
questions.explain: Go home (no preposition). Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: Which sentence means you entered the building?
wrongReasons: ‘To’ only says it was your destination.
questions.explain: ‘Into’ shows entering. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: She got        the taxi outside the hotel.
wrongReasons: ‘Off’ is for buses and trains, not taxis.
questions.explain: Leaving a car or taxi: get out of. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: Get        the bus — it’s leaving!
wrongReasons: ‘In the bus’ is wrong for getting on.
questions.explain: Getting on public transport: get on. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: We pushed our way        the crowd.
questions.explain: Inside a mass of people: through. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: The children ran        the hill shouting.
questions.explain: To a lower place: down. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: The Earth goes        the Sun.
questions.explain: In a circle: round / around. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: The cat hid        the car.
questions.explain: Below something: under. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

questions.text: They built a new bridge        the river.
questions.explain: From one bank to the other: across. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong (if a word is missing, tap the word right after the gap). Twenty original sentences.

items.message: Movement inside: ‘into the house’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
A destination takes ‘to’: ‘flew to Rome’.
Getting onto public transport: ‘get on the bus’.
Taxis take ‘out of’: ‘got out of the taxi’.
Side to side over water: ‘across’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Inside a space with trees: ‘through’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Inside a tunnel: ‘through’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
A road is a flat surface: ‘across’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Water is a space: ‘into the pool’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
A table is a surface: ‘onto’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
To the other side: ‘across’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Balls roll to lower places: ‘down’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Buses take ‘on’: ‘Get on the bus’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Hitting something: ‘crashed into a tree’.
Entering via a door: ‘through the door’.
Boats go below bridges: ‘under’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Destination: ‘to Madrid’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Destination: ‘to school’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Following a street: ‘along’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
British English: ‘towards’ (American: ‘toward’).

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, which direction, multiple choice and spot-the-mistake. In the typing questions write the preposition of movement. One pass, then a breakdown of where you’re strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: He walked {{blank}} the shop to buy bread.
items.explain: Entering a space from outside: into the shop.
From one side of a flat area to the other: across.

items.sentText: The ball went {{blank}} the window and broke it.
items.explain: From one side of an opening to the other: through.
Away from a surface or seat: off. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

items.text: A tunnel, a forest, a crowd → you go…
items.explain: Spaces with sides → through. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

items.text: A road, a bridge, a field → you go…
items.explain: Flat surfaces → across. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

items.text: A bus, a train, a plane → you get…
wrongReasons: ‘Into / out of’ is for cars and taxis.
items.explain: Public transport → get on / off. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

items.text: A car, a taxi → you get…
wrongReasons: ‘On / off’ is for buses and trains.
items.explain: Cars and taxis → get into / out of. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

items.text: She took the keys {{blank}} her bag.
items.explain: From inside → out of. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

items.text: We drove {{blank}} your house but you weren’t there.
items.explain: Going by → past. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Walk home (no preposition). Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

items.text: The plane was flying {{blank}} the airport.
wrongReasons: ‘Into the airport’ means crashing into it.
items.explain: In the direction of → towards. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).

items.message: Movement inside water: ‘into the sea’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
A destination takes ‘to’: ‘walks to work’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
A bridge: ‘across’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
Cars: ‘get out of the car’. Draw the arrow: entering (into), crossing a surface (across), passing inside a space (through).
